messages:
maya: quick thread — I ran an experiment to decouple prefill vs decode lanes + a small "queue shim" on canary. overall token throughput up, but saw KV cache eviction spikes that blow up prefill tail in mixed workloads.

zach: can you paste the replay config / logs? which models and traffic mix?

maya: ran a 30m replay of prod-mix (chat streaming ~60%, single-shot ~40%). TL;DR: prefill p50 82ms -> 68ms, decode p50 35ms -> 30ms, BUT prefill p99 increased ~1.8x when kv_slab_util crosses ~0.6. snippet: 

```
kv_slab_util: 0.45 -> 0.72 during bursts
queue_shim: prefill_slots=4 decode_slots=8
token_budget_targets: prefill=256 decode=48
```

liam: interesting — I also saw a kernel fallback on the long-context model that correlates with the p99. the runtime estimated workspace wrong and fell back to fp32_gemm for big seqs, which added ~200–300ms per call and pushed KV eviction.

sana: my gut: we decoupled lanes but didn't put strong enough admission/backspressure between them. propose: 
1) kernel pinning policy for long-seq quantized models (avoid late fallback)
2) enforce token_budget max per-route per-lane (hard cap)
3) KV drain backpressure earlier (kv_drain_threshold -> 0.55)
4) add metric tag `lane=prefill|decode` and sample tracing id so we can join traces to KV events

maya: plan for canary: push config to 10% traffic with kernel_pin=true, kv_drain_threshold=0.55, token budgets as above, enable lane tagging and 1% trace sampling. deploy-bot: kicked off canary deploy at 1751237890.

deploy-bot: canary deploy (decouple-lanes-v2) started 1751237890 -> completed 1751237922 on canary hosts.

perf-bot: post-canary summary after 1h: overall p50 reduced, p99 prefill down 12% in aggregate, but one backend shard exhibited p99 regressions correlated with kernel fallback. notable log: 

```
[2025-09-02T15:01:12Z] model=long-context-v2 kernel=fallback=fp32_gemm seq=2048 time=342ms
```

zach: two action items from that: 1) add a workspace check at admission time so we never schedule a prefill into a kernel that will fall back late, 2) throttle prefill admission when kv_slab_util > configured threshold (0.55). both cheap to add.

liam: I'm on the kernel workspace check. I can add an estimate pass in the admission path and reject+fallback to different scheduling (or route to a different pool) before we allocate KV slots. will need an opt-in flag for the canary.

sana: I'll iterate the queue_shim to enforce token budgets and put a short hold window when kv_drain is high (like 250ms hold per offending route). also adding metric dashboards: `lane`, `kv_slab_util`, `kernel_fallback_count`.

maya: opened issue #4598 with the experiment result, assigned liam (kernel) + sana (queue_shim) and tagged perf team. notes in the issue include the canary logs and a script to reproduce the replay. :thumbsup:

zach: agreed — once kernel workspace check lands, we should re-run a 60m replay and validate p99 across shards + the kv_slab_util distribution. if stable, ramp to 50%.

maya: thanks all. small follow-ups: add canary label to the traces so we can filter in datadog, and add a health-check that returns `kv_slab_util` in /health for quick debugging.

perf-bot: metric alerts temporarily muted for the canary group.

maya: closing loop here — will post follow-up with replay results after the next canary.
